fatal_errors: The proposed composition-to-property GNN does not reconstruct the target MTP-plus-FEP free-energy methodology.
None of the cited evidence demonstrates GNN prediction of melting or fusion properties, supports the claimed less-than-10% error, or validates transfer across the HEA family.

The hypothesis omits phase-specific free-energy calculations and key physical contributions such as electronic excitations, solid-state short-range order, pressure, exchange-correlation functional dependence, and solid-liquid coexistence.
The baseline is merely experimental data rather than a competing computational method, so efficiency and accuracy improvements cannot be established.
The outputs are not constrained to obey thermodynamic identities, such as entropy of fusion equaling enthalpy of fusion divided by melting temperature at equilibrium.
explanation: The hypothesis names nearly all requested observables, so it has good topical alignment, but it replaces the target physics-based approach with a generic supervised-learning proposal. It provides no relevant temperature, pressure, composition, supercell, or electronic-structure conditions and does not recover the MTP phase-space fidelity, FEP convergence rationale, electronic and SRO corrections, or quantitative performance targets of the hidden work. Its proposed held-out test is directionally falsifiable, but the 10% prediction claim and 20% falsification threshold are arbitrary, leave an unresolved intermediate range, and lack composition-family extrapolation splits, uncertainty calibration, and comparison against CALPHAD or free-energy baselines. The cited studies discuss nanoparticle thermal evolution, phase decomposition, and CALPHAD screening; they do not support the GNN architecture or its claimed accuracy. Thus the proposal is conceivable as a research direction but is not evidence-supported and cannot answer the requested accurate, physically grounded determination of fusion thermodynamics.
